Write \(\frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-2}{-2}=\frac{z-3}{2}=\lambda\). The direction vector is \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), so \(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3\).
Any point on the line is \(P(1+\lambda,\ 2-2\lambda,\ 3+2\lambda)\).
The base point is \(A(1,2,3)\), so
\(\overline{AP}=(\lambda)\hat{i}+(-2\lambda)\hat{j}+(2\lambda)\hat{k}\).
\(|\overline{AP}|=\sqrt{\lambda^2+4\lambda^2+4\lambda^2}=\sqrt{9\lambda^2}=3|\lambda|\).
Given that the distance is \(3\) units, \(3|\lambda|=3\Rightarrow\lambda=\pm 1\).
For \(\lambda=1:\ P=(2,\ 0,\ 5)\).
For \(\lambda=-1:\ P=(0,\ 4,\ 1)\).
\(\therefore\) the required points on the line are \((2,0,5)\) and \((0,4,1)\).

Write \(\frac{x+3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+4}{3}=\lambda\). Any point on the line is \(M(-3+5\lambda,\ 1+2\lambda,\ -4+3\lambda)\) and the direction vector is \(\bar{b}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
Let \(P(0,2,3)\) be the given point. Then
\(\overline{PM}=(5\lambda-3)\hat{i}+(2\lambda-1)\hat{j}+(3\lambda-7)\hat{k}\).
For the foot of the perpendicular, \(\overline{PM}\perp\bar{b}\), i.e. \(\overline{PM}\cdot\bar{b}=0\):
\(5(5\lambda-3)+2(2\lambda-1)+3(3\lambda-7)=0\)
\(25\lambda-15+4\lambda-2+9\lambda-21=0\)
\(38\lambda-38=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1\).
\(\therefore M=(-3+5,\ 1+2,\ -4+3)=(2,\ 3,\ -1)\).
The co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular are \((2,3,-1)\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k},\ \bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{a_2}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k},\ \bar{b_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&-1&1\\1&1&-2\end{vmatrix}=(2-1)\hat{i}-(-4-1)\hat{j}+(2+1)\hat{k}=\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(1)(1)+(1)(5)+(-2)(3)=1+5-6=0\).
Hence the shortest distance \(d=\dfrac{|0|}{|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|}=0\). Since \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\neq\bar{0}\), the lines are not parallel.
\(\therefore\) the lines intersect each other.

For \(\frac{x-5}{4}=\frac{y-7}{5}=\frac{z+3}{5}\): \(\bar{a_1}=5\hat{i}+7\hat{j}-3\hat{k},\ \bar{b_1}=4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).
For \(x-6=y-8=z+2\) (all denominators \(1\)): \(\bar{a_2}=6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-2\hat{k},\ \bar{b_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\4&5&5\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=(5-5)\hat{i}-(4-5)\hat{j}+(4-5)\hat{k}=0\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(1)(0)+(1)(1)+(1)(-1)=0\).
So the shortest distance \(d=0\), and since \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\neq\bar{0}\) the lines are not parallel.
\(\therefore\) the lines intersect each other.

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k},\ \bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{a_2}=2\hat{i}-m\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\ \bar{b_2}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
The lines intersect \(\Rightarrow (\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&3&4\\1&2&1\end{vmatrix}=(3-8)\hat{i}-(2-4)\hat{j}+(4-3)\hat{k}=-5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+(1-m)\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(1)(-5)+(1-m)(2)+(1)(1)=-5+2-2m+1=-2-2m\).
For intersection: \(-2-2m=0\Rightarrow m=-1\).
\(\therefore m=-1\).

Write \(\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-3}{3}=\frac{z+1}{-1}=\lambda\). A general point on the line is \(M(-1+2\lambda,\ 3+3\lambda,\ -1-\lambda)\); direction \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
Let \(P(2,-3,1)\). Then
\(\overline{PM}=(2\lambda-3)\hat{i}+(3\lambda+6)\hat{j}+(-\lambda-2)\hat{k}\).
For the foot of the perpendicular, \(\overline{PM}\cdot\bar{b}=0\):
\(2(2\lambda-3)+3(3\lambda+6)-1(-\lambda-2)=0\)
\(4\lambda-6+9\lambda+18+\lambda+2=0\)
\(14\lambda+14=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-1\).
Foot \(M=(-1-2,\ 3-3,\ -1+1)=(-3,\ 0,\ 0)\).
\(\overline{PM}=(-3-2)\hat{i}+(0+3)\hat{j}+(0-1)\hat{k}=-5\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
Length of the perpendicular \(=|\overline{PM}|=\sqrt{25+9+1}=\sqrt{35}\) units.

The line is \(\bar{r}=(11\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-8\hat{k})+\lambda(10\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-11\hat{k})\), so a general point is \(M(11+10\lambda,\ -2-4\lambda,\ -8-11\lambda)\); direction \(\bar{b}=10\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-11\hat{k}\).
Let \(P(2,-1,5)\) (i.e. \(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\)). Then
\(\overline{PM}=(9+10\lambda)\hat{i}+(-1-4\lambda)\hat{j}+(-13-11\lambda)\hat{k}\).
For the foot of the perpendicular, \(\overline{PM}\cdot\bar{b}=0\):
\(10(9+10\lambda)-4(-1-4\lambda)-11(-13-11\lambda)=0\)
\(90+100\lambda+4+16\lambda+143+121\lambda=0\)
\(237\lambda+237=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-1\).
Foot \(M=(11-10,\ -2+4,\ -8+11)=(1,\ 2,\ 3)\).
\(\overline{PM}=(1-2)\hat{i}+(2+1)\hat{j}+(3-5)\hat{k}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
Length of the perpendicular \(=\sqrt{1+9+4}=\sqrt{14}\) units.
\(\therefore\) foot of perpendicular \(=(1,2,3)\) and length \(=\sqrt{14}\) units.

Write \(\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{-3}=\frac{z+10}{8}=\lambda\). A general point on the line is \(M(1+2\lambda,\ -1-3\lambda,\ -10+8\lambda)\); direction \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\).
Let \(P(1,0,0)\). Then
\(\overline{PM}=(2\lambda)\hat{i}+(-1-3\lambda)\hat{j}+(-10+8\lambda)\hat{k}\).
For the foot of the perpendicular, \(\overline{PM}\cdot\bar{b}=0\):
\(2(2\lambda)-3(-1-3\lambda)+8(-10+8\lambda)=0\)
\(4\lambda+3+9\lambda-80+64\lambda=0\)
\(77\lambda-77=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1\).
Foot \(M=(1+2,\ -1-3,\ -10+8)=(3,\ -4,\ -2)\).
\(\overline{PM}=2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\), so the perpendicular distance \(=\sqrt{4+16+4}=\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt{6}\) units.
\(\therefore\) perpendicular distance \(=2\sqrt{6}\) units and foot of perpendicular \(=(3,-4,-2)\).

The foot \(D\) lies on line \(BC\). \(\overline{BC}=C-B=(2-0)\hat{i}+(-3+11)\hat{j}+(1-13)\hat{k}=2\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-12\hat{k}\).
Let \(D=B+t\,\overline{BC}=(2t,\ -11+8t,\ 13-12t)\).
\(\overline{AD}=D-A=(2t-1)\hat{i}+(8t-11)\hat{j}+(9-12t)\hat{k}\).
Since \(AD\perp BC\), \(\overline{AD}\cdot\overline{BC}=0\):
\(2(2t-1)+8(8t-11)-12(9-12t)=0\)
\(4t-2+64t-88-108+144t=0\)
\(212t-198=0\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{99}{106}\).
Hence
\(x=2t=\dfrac{99}{53},\quad y=-11+8t=-\dfrac{187}{53},\quad z=13-12t=\dfrac{95}{53}\).
\(\therefore D=\left(\dfrac{99}{53},\ -\dfrac{187}{53},\ \dfrac{95}{53}\right)\).
(Note: with the printed data the foot comes out in fractions with denominator \(53\); if integer co-ordinates are expected, the given co-ordinates of \(B\) and \(C\) should be re-checked.)

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j},\ \bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{a_2}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j},\ \bar{b_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&0&1\\1&1&-1\end{vmatrix}=(0-1)\hat{i}-(-2-1)\hat{j}+(2-0)\hat{k}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{1+9+4}=\sqrt{14}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+0\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(1)(-1)+(0)(3)+(0)(2)=-1\).
Shortest distance \(d=\dfrac{|-1|}{\sqrt{14}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{14}}{14}\) units.
Since \(d\neq 0\), the lines do not intersect (they are skew).

For \(\frac{x-5}{4}=\frac{y-7}{-5}=\frac{z+3}{-5}\): \(\bar{a_1}=5\hat{i}+7\hat{j}-3\hat{k},\ \bar{b_1}=4\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\).
For \(\frac{x-8}{7}=\frac{y-7}{1}=\frac{z-5}{3}\): \(\bar{a_2}=8\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k},\ \bar{b_2}=7\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\4&-5&-5\\7&1&3\end{vmatrix}=(-15+5)\hat{i}-(12+35)\hat{j}+(4+35)\hat{k}=-10\hat{i}-47\hat{j}+39\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{100+2209+1521}=\sqrt{3830}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=3\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(3)(-10)+(0)(-47)+(8)(39)=-30+312=282\).
Shortest distance \(d=\dfrac{|282|}{\sqrt{3830}}=\dfrac{282}{\sqrt{3830}}\approx 4.56\) units.
Since \(d\neq 0\), the lines do not intersect (they are skew).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k},\ \bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{a_2}=3\hat{i}+k\hat{j}+0\hat{k},\ \bar{b_2}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
The lines intersect \(\Rightarrow (\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&3&4\\1&2&1\end{vmatrix}=(3-8)\hat{i}-(2-4)\hat{j}+(4-3)\hat{k}=-5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=2\hat{i}+(k+1)\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(2)(-5)+(k+1)(2)+(-1)(1)=-10+2k+2-1=2k-9\).
For intersection: \(2k-9=0\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{9}{2}\).
\(\therefore k=\dfrac{9}{2}\).
